predecessors.name: Southern Wu (Yang Wu)
predecessors.text: the Wu realm Xu Zhigao took over in 937: Cliopatria's Southern Wu 911 shape, which the southern-wu dossier reads as southern Anhui and Jiangsu, Jiangxi and eastern Hubei

successors.name: Song dynasty (Northern and Southern Song)
successors.text: the realm after 958: the Wu realm and Jianzhou and Tingzhou without Huainan, that is the land south of the Yangtze ('forced to cede their territories north of the Yangtze')

ledger.x: October 937: Xu Zhigao takes the Wu realm and founds the Southern Tang.
February 939: Li Bian renames his realm Great Tang.
945: the Southern Tang moves against the Min.
2 October 945: Jianzhou falls, as the page says.
2 October 945: the Southern Tang takes Jianzhou and Tingzhou from the Min.
951: Ma Xi'e of Chu becomes a Southern Tang vassal.
December 951: Ma Xi'e is deposed and Chu ends.
December 951: the Southern Tang takes Chu's Hunan.
952: Chu's former troops turn on the Southern Tang.
Early 956: the Later Zhou invade Huainan.
958: Huainan passes to the Later Zhou.
November 974: Cao Bin opens the Song campaign.
January 976: the remaining Southern Tang passes to the Song.
January 976: the Southern Tang ends with Li Yu's surrender.

wars.name: Southern Tang conquest of Min
wars.outcome: Jianzhou fell on 2 October 945; the Southern Tang kept Jianzhou and Tingzhou, Wuyue secured Fuzhou.

wars.name: Southern Tang conquest of Chu
wars.outcome: Chu was subjugated in December 951; Liu Yan and former Chu troops expelled the Southern Tang from Hunan by 1 December 952.

wars.name: Southern Han seizure of Chu's Lingnan lands
wars.outcome: 'Liu Sheng launched a successful invasion to secure Lingnan'; the Southern Tang counterattack 'ended in failure' and the Southern Han kept the land.

wars.name: Later Zhou invasion of Huainan
wars.outcome: Shouchun fell by April 958; the Southern Tang ceded all territory north of the Yangtze and became a Later Zhou vassal.

wars.name: Song conquest of Southern Tang
wars.outcome: Cao Bin's campaign (November 974) crossed the Yangtze at Caishiji, besieged Jinling from April 975 and took the surrender of Li Yu in January 976; Wuyue forces joined the siege.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes a Southern Tang border.
